showFullCode.title: Show Complete File
showFullCode.description: Show complete file for code, with bootstrap and error handling included.

AiBriefHttpRequest.title: AiBriefHttpRequest
AiBriefHttpRequest.description: What the console may send: the stage and, for disputes, which case. Session facts are never caller input.

AupCategorySignalResponse.title: AupCategorySignalResponse
AupCategorySignalResponse.description: Optional Channel3 signal shown next to the AUP result; it never changes the rule decision.

CaseRouteResponse.title: CaseRouteResponse
CaseRouteResponse.description: Fuzzy case routing: which goods group (and so which dispute items) applies. Code decides; advisory only.

ConnectionsResponse.title: ConnectionsResponse
ConnectionsResponse.description: Deployment mode only. Never a key, a key's presence, a value or a variable name.

CountryRulesCheckRequest.title: CountryRulesCheckRequest
CountryRulesCheckRequest.description: Seller and buyer countries plus closed choices; no free text reaches the check.

ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody
ErrorBody.description: The error body every refusal uses.

GuideFormRequest.title: GuideFormRequest
GuideFormRequest.description: One field ({item, value}) or one round of up to three fields ({fields: [...]}), never both.

ProductCard.title: ProductCard
ProductCard.description: A Channel3 catalogue product reduced to what identifies the item; no prices, offers or buy links.

ProductConfirmResponse.title: ProductConfirmResponse
ProductConfirmResponse.description: The seller's own choice: one of the cards they were shown, or none of them.

ProductReferenceResponse.title: ProductReferenceResponse
ProductReferenceResponse.description: Up to three Channel3 products for the seller to pick from; advisory, never changes the AUP decision.

SendGuard.title: SendGuard
SendGuard.description: (r25 send guard) What a send carries and to whom, side by side; every account id is masked (first 2, last 4).

SyntheticMoney.title: SyntheticMoney
SyntheticMoney.description: Same shape as the PayPal Disputes `dispute_amount` (ProviderMoney below); values are synthetic.

WebhookEventProjection.title: WebhookEventProjection
WebhookEventProjection.description: All that is kept after a SUCCESS: identifiers and status only, no amounts, payer data, links or summary.

code.description: Stable machine-readable reason, for example session_required.

message.description: A plain sentence for a person.

Title: Getting Started with TradeGlot Local Console

Nodes.Text: API of the local TradeGlot console (127.0.0.1:8000). It uses synthetic data, expects the demo session headers the console sets, and the hosted demo answers 503 on every route that would reach PayPal.
The generated code depends on a few Ruby gems. The references to these gems are added in the gemspec file. The easiest way to resolve the dependencies, build the gem and install it is through Rake:

1. Install Rake if not already installed: `gem install rake`
  2. Install Bundler if not already installed: `gem install bundler`
  3. From terminal/cmd navigate to the root directory of the SDK.
  4. Invoke: `rake install`
Alternatively, you can build and install the gem manually:

1. From terminal/cmd navigate to the root directory of the SDK.
  2. Run the build command: `gem build trade_glot_local_console.gemspec`
  3. Run the install command: `gem install trade_glot_local_console-0.2.0.gem`

The following section explains how to use the trade_glot_local_console ruby gem in a new Rails project using RubyMine™. The basic workflow presented here is also applicable if you prefer using a different editor or IDE.
Close any existing projects in RubyMine™ by selecting `File -> Close Project`. Next, click on `Create New Project` to create a new project from scratch.

Nodes.AlternateText: Create a new project in RubyMine - Step 1

Nodes.Text: Next, provide `TestApp` as the project name, choose `Rails Application` as the project type, and click `OK`.

Nodes.AlternateText: Create a new Rails Application in RubyMine - Step 2

Nodes.Text: In the next dialog make sure that the correct Ruby SDK is being used (>= 2.6 and <= 3.2) and click `OK`.

Nodes.AlternateText: Create a new Rails Application in RubyMine - Step 3

Nodes.Text: In order to use the `trade_glot_local_console` gem in the new project we must add a gem reference. Locate the `Gemfile` in the Project Explorer window under the `TestApp` project node. The file contains references to all gems being used in the project. Here, add the reference to the library gem by adding the following line: `gem 'trade_glot_local_console', '0.2.0'`

Nodes.AlternateText: Add new reference to the Gemfile

Nodes.Text: Once the `TestApp` project is created, a folder named `controllers` will be visible in the *Project Explorer* under the following path: `TestApp > app > controllers`. Right click on this folder and select `New -> Run Rails Generator...`.

Nodes.AlternateText: Run Rails Generator on Controllers Folder

Nodes.Text: Selecting the said option will popup a small window where the generator names are displayed. Here, select the `controller` template.
Next, a popup window will ask you for a Controller name and included Actions. For controller name provide `Hello` and include an action named `Index` and click `OK`.
A new controller class named `HelloController` will be created in a file named `hello_controller.rb` containing a method named `Index`.

1. Add the `require 'trade_glot_local_console'` statement to require the gem in the controller file.
  2. Add the `include TradeGlotLocalConsole` statement to include the sdk module in the controller file.
  3. In the `Index` method, add code for initialization and a sample for its usage.

Code-Based Client Initialization

require 'trade_glot_local_console'

client = Client.new
Environment-Based Client Initialization

Nodes.Title: Use the rule checks from an AI agent (MCP)

Nodes.Text: The repository ships a small read-only MCP server, `src/payguard/mcp_server.py`, built on the Python standard library. It speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio.

| Tool | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `check_acceptable_use` | A review signal for a product description. |
| `list_countries` | The ten countries in the rules pack. |
| `check_country_rules` | Findings for a seller and buyer country, most severe first, each with its source. |
| `search_rule_clauses` | The best matches among 140 paraphrased PayPal clauses. |
| `check_sales_spike` | A comparison with a baseline you declare; the answer says the baseline is unverified. |
There is no tool that sends evidence, connects to PayPal, approves or changes anything.
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -B -m payguard.mcp_server

Nodes.Title: What TradeGlot is, and what it is not

Nodes.Text: TradeGlot gives small PayPal sellers rule checks and a gated evidence workflow. Everything in this API documentation describes the **local console** (127.0.0.1:8000) and runs on **synthetic data** against the **PayPal Sandbox**.

- Advisory only: every answer is a review signal. It is not a compliance decision and not legal advice.
- A person approves every send: one tick, then two presses. The hosted demo makes no PayPal calls and answers `503 hosted_demo_disabled` on every route that would.
- The AI step (Gemini) only picks from closed options and its picks are checked by rules. It does not guess and does not decide who wins.
- PayPal and the card issuer make every real decision.

- Browse the endpoint groups on the left. Each one says whether the hosted demo answers it.
- Agents can use the same rule checks through the read-only MCP server: see the next guide.
Evidence brief (local console with a model profile only).

Nodes.Text: Represents the proxy server configurations for API calls.
Properties

Data: The port to connect to the proxy server.

CodeExamples.Title: Usage Example
CodeExamples.Text:
require 'trade_glot_local_console'
include TradeGlotLocalConsole


client = TradeGlotLocalConsole::Client.new(
  proxy_settings: ProxySettings.new(
    address: "http://localhost",
    port: 8888,
    username: 'user',
    password: 'pass'
  )
)

Nodes.Text: The SDK client can also be initialized directly from environment variables using the `from_env` class method. This allows the SDK to automatically read configuration values from the runtime environment or a `.env` file.

require 'trade_glot_local_console'
include TradeGlotLocalConsole

# Create client from environment
client = Client.from_env

You can also load values from a `.env` file before creating the client.
To do this, install and use the dotenv
 gem:
gem install dotenv

Now require 'dotenv/load' automatically loads all variables from a `.env` file into `ENV`,
so the `from_env` method can access them.

require 'dotenv/load'
require 'trade_glot_local_console'
include TradeGlotLocalConsole

# Create client from environment
client = Client.from_env
The same method can accept keyword arguments to override any values read from the environment.

# To override or fill in values that are not set in the environment, pass them
# as keyword arguments when calling `from_env`
client = Client.from_env(environment: 'production', timeout: 30)
Values provided through arguments take precedence over those defined in environment variables.
Example .env File

ENVIRONMENT='production'


TIMEOUT=60
MAX_RETRIES=3
BACKOFF_FACTOR=2
RETRY_INTERVAL=1
RETRY_STATUSES=408,413
RETRY_METHODS=GET,PUT,DELETE
PROXY_ADDRESS='http://localhost:3000'
PROXY_PORT=8080
PROXY_USERNAME='username'
PROXY_PASSWORD='password'
Note
- If an environment variable is not defined, the default SDK configuration value will be used.
